name: Calendar Intelligence - Meeting Briefs Tailored By Meeting Type

parameters.content:
## Calendar Intelligence
Briefs before your meetings - but a sales call, a recurring 1:1, an interview and an internal sync are four different jobs, so this treats them as four different jobs rather than sending the same template for all of them.

## Five ways a meeting gets handled
- **Interview** - candidate focused: what previous rounds already covered, what is still unknown, what to open with
- **Recurring** - what was left open at the end of last time, not a fresh brief every week
- **Internal** - three lines. Purpose and your part. No research, no email dredging.
- **External with history** - where you left off, open threads, what to raise
- **External, first contact** - explicitly a cold first meeting: what to establish, no invented relationship

## How it works
1. Runs every 30 minutes, or on demand
2. Pulls the next 4 hours of calendar, drops anything already briefed, cancelled, declined, or outside the window
3. Classifies each meeting by title keywords, attendee domains, and whether this series has been briefed before
4. Routes to the matching handler - only two of the five hit Gmail, the others do not need to
5. One AI step writes to whichever instruction its handler produced
6. Sends and logs, storing the brief so the next occurrence can diff against it

## Setup
- [ ] Connect Google Calendar, Gmail and Google Sheets credentials
- [ ] Open Brief Config: calendar ID, where briefs go, your internal domain(s), lead time, and the words that mean 'interview' to you
- [ ] Create a spreadsheet with a **Briefed** tab and these headers:
      Briefed At, Event ID, Series ID, Meeting, Starts At, Attendees, Type, Brief
- [ ] Point both Google Sheets nodes at it
- [ ] Activate

## Customize
Set BriefInternalMeetings to false to skip internal syncs entirely. Add words to InterviewKeywords to catch your own naming. The Brief column is what makes recurring deltas work - do not remove it.

nodes.name: Sticky Note - Why Store The Brief

parameters.content: **The log is not just dedupe.** It stores the Series ID and the full brief text, which is what lets a recurring meeting be briefed as 'here is what was still open last time' instead of starting from zero every week. Clearing that sheet costs you the recurring memory, not just the dedupe.

## 1. Select, then classify
Four filters decide what is worth briefing at all. Whatever survives gets a type - based on title keywords, whether any attendee is outside your domains, and whether this recurring series has been briefed before.

## 2. Five handlers, genuinely different work
Interview and external hit Gmail for real history. Recurring reads the previous brief instead. Internal does neither - it needs no research and an internal sync does not warrant an AI trawl of your inbox. Each produces its own instruction for the writer.

## 3. Write, send, remember
One AI node serves all five handlers - the instruction it receives is what differs, not the model. The brief is stored so the next occurrence of a recurring meeting can build on it.
